why.FLAT.3: The champion FLAT.3, Leukocytoclastic vasculitis, is the best explanation for the observed case due to the presence of painful lesions on both legs, elevated C-reactive protein, increased erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and histopathological findings of intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with marked papillary dermal edema, necrosis of vessel walls, and focal fibrinoid necrosis, which are consistent with the characteristics of leukocytoclastic vasculitis.

sub_branches.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
sub_branches.why_included: The patient's presentation of painful lesions on both legs, which ulcerated several days after appearance, is consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum. The patient's history of treatment with methimazole and atenolol, as well as the presence of pitting edema and multiple discrete, round, dry ulcers with central eschars, dusky gray borders, and collarettes of scale, also support this diagnosis.
